dialogue.content: 本日はよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in today. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: そうぞよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.content: お時間になりましたら始めさせて頂きます。
dialogue.English: We'll begin now that it's our scheduled time.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: こんにちは相談員です。本日はお越し頂きありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm your counselor. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: はじめにあなたの年齢と性別をお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.English: To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Of course.

dialogue.content: 40歳、女性です
dialogue.English: I'm 40 years old, female.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。本日はどのようなご相談でしたでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. What brought you in for counseling today?

dialogue.content: 息子が20歳なのですが、引きこもってしまっていて、社会に出ていくのはまだまだ無理そうで困っています。
dialogue.English: My 20-year-old son has become a shut-in, and I'm worried because it seems impossible for him to re-enter society anytime soon.

dialogue.content: 母としてどうしたらよいものか・・・
dialogue.English: As his mother, I just don't know what to do...

dialogue.content: 息子さんのご心配について、お話しに来てくださったんですね。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: So you've come to talk about your concerns for your son. Thank you for sharing that.

dialogue.content: ご心配ですよね。
dialogue.English: It must be very worrying for you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ご相談者様としましては、息子さんにどのようになって欲しいかお聞かせいただけますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me what you hope for your son?

dialogue.content: 今はまだ、やりたいことが見つからないみたいで、何をすればどうすればわからない。と言っていますが、少しずつ社会とかかわって自立してほしいと思っています。私はシングルですので息子をずっと面倒みられるわけではないすし
dialogue.English: Right now, it seems he hasn't found what he wants to do yet, and he says he doesn't know what to do. I hope he can gradually engage with society and become independent. I'm a single mother, so I won't be able to take care of him forever.

dialogue.content: お一人で、息子さんの子育てを頑張っていらっしゃったのですね。
dialogue.English: So you've been working hard to raise your son on your own.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、現在何か社会と関わる行動をされようとはしていますか？（働こうとしている等）
dialogue.English: Is your son currently taking any steps to engage with society, such as looking for work?

dialogue.content: 2年前に離婚したので、一人で育てたわけではいし、息子と元旦那は今でもつながっています。父親がいない子供とは少し違う状況です。
dialogue.English: I got divorced two years ago, so it's not like I raised him all by myself. My son and my ex-husband are still in touch, so his situation is a bit different from that of a child without a father.

dialogue.content: 息子にはアルバイトしてみるとか、、、と促していた時期もあるのですが、
dialogue.English: There was a time when I encouraged him to try getting a part-time job or something, but...

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。元旦那様には、息子さんについてご相談されたりしますか？
dialogue.English: I see. Do you ever discuss your son with your ex-husband?

dialogue.content: 無理そうで、では通信制の大学なども進めてみたのですが、土壇場になってできない、ということになり出願するのを断念して。今は間にもできない状況です。
dialogue.English: That seemed impossible, so I also suggested things like a correspondence university, but at the last minute, he would say he couldn't do it, and we had to give up on applying. Right now, he's in a state where he can't do anything.

dialogue.content: 何もできない状況です。
dialogue.English: He's in a state where he can't do anything.

dialogue.content: 元旦那とは、、、どうでしょう
dialogue.English: As for my ex-husband... I'm not sure.

dialogue.content: お母様も、一生懸命お考えになられているのですね。
dialogue.English: You've been thinking very hard about this as well, haven't you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、お友達と遊びに行ったりはされますか？
dialogue.English: Does your son ever go out with friends?

dialogue.content: いえ、、引きこもりですので。。。友達はいないと思います。犬の散歩に出るくらいです。
dialogue.English: No... since he's a shut-in, I don't think he has any friends. The only time he goes out is to walk the dog.

dialogue.content: それは、お母様としても心配ですね…
dialogue.English: That must be very worrying for you as his mother.

dialogue.content: ほんとうに、どうしたらよいのか
dialogue.English: I really don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、引きこまれてどれ位になりますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: How long has your son been withdrawn like this?

dialogue.content: 高校2年生で不登校になり、それからですので4・５年です
dialogue.English: He stopped going to school in his second year of high school, so it's been about four or five years since then.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。息子さんが不登校になった原因について、お母様はご存知でしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. Do you happen to know why he stopped going to school?

dialogue.content: それでも、大検は取ったので、勉強は嫌いではないし知識はいろいろあるみたいで、色々教えられます
dialogue.English: Even so, he passed the high school equivalency exam, so he doesn't dislike studying. He seems to be knowledgeable about many things and often teaches me.

dialogue.content: うーん、はっきりしたことはわかりません。
dialogue.English: Hmm, I don't know for sure.

dialogue.content: 息子さん、大検取られるなんて素晴らしいですね。
dialogue.English: It's wonderful that your son passed the high school equivalency exam.

dialogue.content: ただ、その辺りで家庭の不和があったのは確かですが、学校で何かあったとかはなさそうですし、原因はわからないです。
dialogue.English: However, it's true that there was some family discord around that time, but it doesn't seem like anything happened at school, so I just don't know the cause.

dialogue.content: お母様としても、原因が分からないのもお辛いですよね…
dialogue.English: It must be painful for you as a mother not to know the cause, as well.

dialogue.content: そうですね、、、最近は原因を追究しても仕方がないと思っています。それより、これからどうしたらよいか・・・
dialogue.English: Yes... Lately, I've come to think that there's no point in pursuing the cause. I'm more concerned about what we should do from now on...

dialogue.content: 息子さんには、人と接することには拒否感はなさそうですか？
dialogue.English: Does your son seem to have any aversion to interacting with people?

dialogue.content: 人と会ったりすることに拒否感はなさそうです。ただ、予定を立てたとして、その予定の前になると急に不安になってきて、あれもできないかもこれもできないかも、と、パニックになってしまう感じです
dialogue.English: He doesn't seem to have an aversion to meeting people. However, if he makes plans, he gets suddenly anxious right before, thinking 'maybe I can't do this, maybe I can't do that,' and it seems like he panics.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。息子さんは、丁寧に１つ１つ受け止めてから、行動される性格なのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. It sounds like he’s the type who needs to carefully process things one by one before taking action.

dialogue.content: そうですね、いろいろ考え込んでしまうタイプ、石橋を叩きすぎで渡れないタイプですね
dialogue.English: Yes, he's the type who overthinks things, so cautious that he can't bring himself to move forward.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。でも大きな失敗はされないという事だと思いますので、その性格の特徴と上手く付き合っていければ良いですね。
dialogue.English: I see. But I imagine that also means he avoids making big mistakes, so it would be good if he could learn to work with that aspect of his personality.

dialogue.content: お母様としましては、やはり将来的に現在のままでは不安だと思われます。
dialogue.English: As his mother, you must feel anxious about the future if things stay as they are.

dialogue.content: 元旦那様と奥様は、今もお話をされる事はありますか？
dialogue.English: Do you and your ex-husband still speak to each other at all?

dialogue.content: いや、離婚してますので話しません、話したくもないです
dialogue.English: No, we're divorced so we don't talk. And I don't want to, either.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 息子さんと、今後についてお話をされた事はありますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Have you talked with your son about his future?

dialogue.content: いつもいつもはなしていました。でも、プレッシャーを与えすぎるのはよくないかなと思って、最近は家のことをやってくれるようになってすごく助かっています。
dialogue.English: We used to talk about it all the time. But I thought it might not be good to put too much pressure on him, and recently he's started helping around the house, which has been a huge help.

dialogue.content: なので、最近はプレッシャーになることはあまり言わないようにしています。
dialogue.English: So lately, I've been trying not to say things that might put pressure on him.

dialogue.content: お母様とのコミュニケーションも良好で、とてもお優しそうな息子さんですね。
dialogue.English: It sounds like he has good communication with you. He seems like a very kind son.

dialogue.content: お話をお聞きしていまして、過度なプレッシャーは確かに息子さんには負担になってしまうかもしれないですね。
dialogue.English: Listening to what you've said, it does seem that excessive pressure might be a burden for your son.

dialogue.content: そう思ってそっとしていますが、はれ物に触るような感じで過ごすのもいつまでつつくのかと思うとしんどいです。
dialogue.English: That's what I've been thinking, so I try to leave him be, but living as if I’m walking on eggshells is exhausting, and I wonder how long it will go on.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。お辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. That must be very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、これをしていると夢中になるという事はございますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is there anything that your son gets completely absorbed in when he's doing it?

dialogue.content: テレビや本は好きみたいですね、いつも何かを読んでいます
dialogue.English: He seems to like TV and books. He's always reading something.

dialogue.content: 読書がお好きなんですね。
dialogue.English: So he enjoys reading.

dialogue.content: そうですね
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: お話をお聞きしていますと、息子さんは優しく、普通にお話をきちんと聞いてくださる方だと思われますので、
dialogue.English: From what you've shared, it sounds like your son is a kind person who listens attentively,

dialogue.content: 食事の時間にでも、
dialogue.English: so perhaps during mealtimes,

dialogue.content: 将来について、話す時間を毎日とってみてはいかがでしょうか？（息子さんが、将来について思われている事を自由に話す時間としてです。）
dialogue.English: how about trying to set aside time every day to talk about the future? (As a time for your son to speak freely about his own thoughts on the matter.)

dialogue.content: 将来について触れないように過ごしているのに、どうやって話せばいいのでしょう
dialogue.English: I've been trying to avoid bringing up the future, so how am I supposed to talk about it?

dialogue.content: 将来について話してと言うのではなく、息子さんが好きな事、やりたい事についてお話するのを聞く事は出来ますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Instead of saying, 'Let's talk about the future,' could you perhaps just listen to him talk about the things he likes and wants to do?

dialogue.content: やりたいことはないそうで、見つけられない自分を責めています。
dialogue.English: He says there's nothing he wants to do, and he blames himself for not being able to find anything.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。息子さんは、ご自身を責めてしまうのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So he tends to blame himself.

dialogue.content: 好きなことはとてもよく話すので、その話を永遠聞いているのは毎日しています。私しか話せる相手がいないので
dialogue.English: He talks a great deal about the things he likes, and I listen to him go on about them every day, since I'm the only person he has to talk to.

dialogue.content: 毎日話を聞いているのも疲れますがね。。。話してくれるだけで今はいいかと思っています
dialogue.English: It's tiring listening to him every day, though... But for now, I suppose it's good that he's talking to me at all.

dialogue.content: そうですね。お話をする相手がいるという事は、息子さんも大きな心の支えになっていると思われます。
dialogue.English: I agree. Having someone to talk to is likely a great source of emotional support for your son.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、お母様と一緒に外出するのに抵抗はございますか？
dialogue.English: Does your son have any resistance to going out with you?

dialogue.content: いえ、外出にはていこうはないです、なので、社会に出られない引きこもりですね
dialogue.English: No, he has no resistance to going out. That's the problem. He's a shut-in in the sense that he can't participate in society.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。すぐ働かれるのは難しいかもしてないので、働く前に職業訓練校に行かれるという選択もあると思うのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. It might be difficult for him to start working right away, so one option could be to attend a vocational training school before getting a job. What do you think about that?

dialogue.content: その訓練に行く前に、あれやこれや悩んで（本人は）前に進めないでいます。ただ、話し相手になることで息子の為になると信じて毎日を過ごすしかないのかなぁと、話していて思いました。
dialogue.English: He would worry about this and that before he could even go to the training, and he wouldn't be able to move forward. As I've been talking to you, I've started to think that maybe all I can do is get through each day believing that just being someone he can talk to is helping him.

dialogue.content: 長い事お付き合いいただきありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you for taking so much time to listen to me.

dialogue.content: お時間になってしまいましたので、ここまでとさせて頂きます。こちらこそありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Our time is up for today, so we'll have to end here. Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: （それではしつれいいたします）
dialogue.English: (Well then, goodbye.)

dialogue.content: （時間過ぎて、本当に申し訳ございません。。本日は、クライアント役ありがとうございました。色々ご指導頂けますよう、よろしくお願いいたします。）
dialogue.English: (I'm so sorry for going over our time. Thank you for playing the role of the client today. I look forward to receiving your guidance and feedback.)
